run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-14T21:08:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is explained by a brief but complete outage of the ad and payment gRPC backends on 2026-11-14. Both `ad` and `payment` deployments carry the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-14T21:07:15Z and were rolled out at that moment: the old pods (ad-554b849958-mbnxm, payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb) were killed at 21:07:18–19 and new single-replica pods ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 were created, with containers started at 21:07:17–18. Neither deployment defines a readinessProbe, so the kubelet marked both pods Ready at 21:07:18/21:07:19 and their pod IPs were placed in the Service Endpoints while the applications were not yet listening on :8080. During that gap, frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds failed with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 'No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080' (the ad ClusterIP), and checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge failed with 'dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused' (the payment ClusterIP), which frontend surfaced as HTTP 500 on GET /api/data and POST /api/checkout. The ad-service GetAds server counter stopped increasing at 1415 from ~21:08 and the new ad container's request logs only begin at 21:15:47 (payment's at 21:14:58), matching the frontend AdService/GetAds error counter rising 421→802 between 21:08:00 and 21:15:30. Errors then stopped: the whole 21:15:08–21:25:08 range shows zero frontend ERROR spans. Frontend itself, its cart and product-catalog paths, cart, currency, product-catalog, quote, shipping, ad and payment application code show no ERROR spans of their own, so the alert reflects dependency unavailability during the rollout rather than a frontend defect. CPU throttling of the new containers (ad CFS throttled ratio ~0.90 against a 50m CPU limit, payment ~0.47 against 20m) is consistent with, but does not by itself prove, the slow application start.

claims.text: In the alert window 20:08:49–21:25:08Z, otel-demo/frontend span ERROR counts (increase over 4579s) were: span_name GET 387.145, GET /api/data 387.145, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 387.145, POST 42.677, POST /api/checkout 42.677, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 42.677, tcp.connect 15.242, while GET /api/cart and POST /api/cart stayed at 0.

Frontend error spans carry HTTP 500 and gRPC status 14: the sampled trace shows frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (span c14ccc4dc332d2d8) with status tags rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and detail '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080', and checkout client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (span 1ed8eee7310c408b) with 'connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused"'.

The refused addresses are the Service ClusterIPs: Service ad is 100.65.180.246 port 8080 targetPort 8080 selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad, Service payment is 100.70.188.60 port 8080 targetPort 8080 selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment, Service frontend is 100.70.149.120.

Namespace otel-demo events show a rollout at 21:07:15–21:07:19Z: Deployment ad 'Scaled up replica set ad-6cb57f76d from 0 to 1' and 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0', SuccessfulCreate/Scheduled/Created/Started ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 (container started 21:07:17), ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 SuccessfulDelete and Pod Killing ad-554b849958-mbnxm at 21:07:18; equivalently for payment (payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 started 21:07:18, payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb killed 21:07:19).

Both restarted Deployments carry pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-14T21:07:15Z, both define readinessProbe=null for their single container, ad has resources limits cpu 50m/memory 450Mi and payment cpu 20m/memory 160Mi, and both use RollingUpdate maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25% at replicas=1.

Pod conditions: ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 is Ready=True since 21:07:18Z and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 Ready=True since 21:07:19Z (both on node i-0e9f8b08cc290a884); frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 has been Ready=True since 20:33:34Z on node i-09cfabe46e9495420.

The cumulative frontend client-span counter traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",span_name="grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} was flat at 421 from 20:50:00 through 21:08:00Z, rose stepwise (433 at 21:08:30, 503, 558, 609, 667, 722, 760) to 802 at 21:15:30, and stayed 802 through the last sample at 21:23:30.

Ad-side GetAds server spans show a serving gap: the series exported_instance=c70d5537-20a8-4caf-976e-83cfc75e9369 stopped at 1415 from the 21:08:30 sample onward, and a series with a different exported_instance (d90a4539-adc4-437f-b0c9-d85e84bcefce) first appears at 21:16:30 with 57, rising to 175 by 21:19:00 and then flat.

The new ad container's request logs in 21:05–21:25Z begin only at 21:15:47.825 ('Targeted ad request received for [accessories]'), i.e. no request-handling lines exist earlier in that window; the newest line read is 21:16:41. The new payment container's logs begin at 21:14:58.223 ('Charge request received.'), newest line 21:16:44. Both containers report 'no previous instance', and all lines are normal request handling with no error lines.

Errors did not continue to the end of the window: for the 600s ending 21:25:08Z (21:15:08–21:25:08Z) the increase of every frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR series was 0 (including GET /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, POST /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, tcp.connect).

Container CFS throttling ratio rose in step with the gap: ad went from a ~0.10–0.15 baseline to 0.232 (21:08:00), 0.539 (21:10:00), 0.904 (21:15:00) and 0.920 (21:17:00); payment went from ~0.15 to 0.219 (21:08:00) and 0.474 (21:15:00). New-pod CPU usage reached ~0.049 cores for ad (limit 50m) and ~0.0143 cores for payment (limit 20m).

Impact seen on other services' own spans in the window: checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 34.83 and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 34.83 ERROR spans; frontend-proxy 'ingress' 454.21 and 'router frontend egress' 429.82 ERROR spans (HTTP 500 responses; in trace 39738559ae15135780326c17f7d13235 the ingress/egress spans are parents of frontend's failing GET). ERROR-span increases for accounting, cart and payment were 0 (ad only flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 1.02); cart/currency/product-catalog/quote/shipping/ad paths called by frontend show 0 ERROR spans for grpc.oteldemo.CartService/* and GET /api/cart.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running with restartCount 0 and empty lastState; only ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 have start times at 21:07:15Z, the others started 20:33–20:35Z. Current ad/payment Endpoints point at those new pods (100.96.4.142 and 100.96.4.221) with single container IDs and ready/started true.

Primary cause: the 21:07:15Z rollout restart replaced the single-replica ad and payment pods; because neither Deployment has a readinessProbe, the new pods were declared Ready at 21:07:18/19 and their IPs entered the Service Endpoints while the applications were still not listening on :8080, so callers' gRPC dials to the ad (100.65.180.246) and payment (100.70.188.60) ClusterIPs were refused until the apps began serving (~21:14:58 payment, ~21:15:47 ad). The frontend error burst (421→802 GetAds errors, 21:08:00–21:15:30) matches that gap and stops once the backends serve.

Contributing mechanism (correlation only): the very low CPU limits (ad 50m, payment 20m) starved application start-up, evidenced by ad CFS throttling rising to ~0.90 and usage pinning at ~0.049 cores during 21:08–21:18 while the process was not yet serving. No container log line records start-up timing, so the causal link to the ~8-minute delay is not directly proven.

Rejected: application-level failure inside ad or payment. Neither service produced ERROR spans in the window (ad's only error series is flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 1.02; payment's GET/tcp.connect/dns.lookup ERROR increases are 0), and the new ad container logs show normal request handling once it starts.

Rejected: a frontend application defect. The failing frontend spans are client spans to ad/payment carrying connection-refused details, GET /api/cart and grpc.oteldemo.CartService/* ERROR counts are 0, the frontend pod has been Ready since 20:33:34Z with no restarts, and frontend errors stop without any frontend change.

Rejected: OOMKill or eviction of the ad/payment pods. No OOMKilled/Evicted event appears among the 18 otel-demo events in the window, all pods are Running with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, and the pod replacements are recorded as Deployment ScalingReplicaSet + ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete.

Checked and healthy during the window: cart (ERROR increases 0 for flagd EventStream/ResolveBoolean and for frontend's grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and GetCart), accounting (orders receive 0), payment service's own spans (GET, tcp.connect, dns.lookup ERROR 0), and ad service's own spans (no ERROR series except a flagd EventStream value of 1.02). In the sampled trace, currency, product-catalog, quote and shipping spans report rpc.grpc.status_code=0 / otel.status_code=OK.

gaps: The Alertmanager rule 'RequestErrorRate' is not retrievable here: list_prometheus_rules returned no data for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and for an unfiltered query, so its expression, threshold and the reported current value 2.5777777777777775 cannot be verified against a metric.

No kube-state-metrics deployment/pod status series exist in this Prometheus (get_metric_names for kube_deployment_status.* / kube_pod_status.* returned nothing), so replica-ready time series for ad/payment could not be used; readiness was taken from pod conditions via the Kubernetes API.
The frontend container produced no readable log lines at all in 21:00–21:25Z (bytes_read 0), so there is no frontend application-log corroboration of the 500 responses.
Jaeger's newest trace data ends at 21:08:23–21:08:24Z; the 21:08:24–21:15:30Z failure interval is only visible through span metrics, pod logs and CPU metrics, not through traces.

change_history is not an integrated source in this run, so what or who issued the kubectl rollout restart at 21:07:15Z (and whether it was remediation for an earlier problem) is unknown; the frontend error counter was flat before 21:08:00, so no pre-restart failure is visible inside the observed window.

Ad and payment container log streams end at 21:16:41Z and 21:16:44Z respectively although ad's GetAds counter kept increasing until 21:19:00; log content after those times is unknown, and ad's counter stops rising after 21:19:00 for reasons not determinable from this evidence.
No trace-level view of the payment side after 21:08:23Z exists, so checkout's PlaceOrder error timing after that instant rests on span-metric counts only.
next_steps: Identify the actor/change record behind kubectl rollout restart of deployments ad and payment at 2026-11-14T21:07:15Z (the restartedAt annotation) from the deployment pipeline or change history, and confirm whether it was planned.

Add readinessProbe (and probably startupProbe) on port 8080 to the ad and payment containers so pods are not put into Service Endpoints before the app listens, and consider raising their CPU limits (ad 50m, payment 20m) so start-up is not throttled.
Consider running more than one replica for ad and payment (or a PodDisruptionBudget-aware rolling update) so a single-pod replacement cannot remove the only backend.

Confirm with Alertmanager that RequestErrorRate has resolved after 21:15:30Z, and check the alert rule expression/threshold in the Prometheus that actually holds it, since it is not present in the queried Prometheus.
